text: The access point will go through this list using the so called polling scheme. The polling scheme, very simple. Let's assume now the first station to poll is A. This means that after SIFS, since the beacon, our access point will send a poll packet, and this poll is intended for A. And this poll packet from the access point, let's say to A, essentially means A. Now you can transmit. Okay. So upon receiving this poll message, A will send its data packet if it has got the data packet to transmit. Okay. Now we don't know, notice that we don't know how long this transmission will be, right? Because it depends on the payload of this data packet, and it depends on the speed at which A will transmit toward the access point. But anyway, it will run. When A finishes after SIFS, the access point will poll the next station in the list. That in our example is C. Now let's consider in this case that the access point has got some data to send to C. So in this case, it will of course.
